title: The Morning Digest: November 23, 2026
dek: UKMTO reported on Sunday evening that a tanker was involved in an incident with military forces in the Gulf of Oman near Chabahar, with the vessel, the forces and any damage unidentified (UKMTO, Nov 22). Iran's Revolutionary Guard Navy said two supertankers struck naval mines north of Ghanam Island and caught fire, a claim with no vessel named and no independent verification. AIS-visible crossings through the strait fell to 2 commercial ships on Sunday, neither of them a tanker (hormuz.now, Nov 23). Brent Jan27 was $92.67 and WTI Jan27 was $83.57 in Asia on Monday (Reuters, Nov 23). January WCS paper settled -$21.65 (ICE TMW settle, Nov 20). The validated diesel crack is $77.66 on the latest print.

sources.vintage: Nov 23, 2026 (overnight tape at 0423 GMT: Brent Jan27 $92.67, up $0.10 or 0.11 percent; WTI Jan27 $83.57, up $0.16 or 0.19 percent; Brent traded down to $91.57 and WTI to $82.63 earlier in the session; at 0216 GMT Brent was $92.29, down 0.30 percent, and WTI was $83.26, down 0.18 percent, in a move tied to an equity selloff with Gulf attacks limiting losses; Friday settles were Brent Jan27 $92.57, up $0.59 and down 3.41 percent on the week, and WTI Jan27 $83.41, up $0.97)

Nov 22, 2026, via euronews and Anadolu (a tanker was involved in an incident with military forces in the Gulf of Oman, east of the strait near Chabahar, reported by a company security officer at 14:25 GMT; the vessel, the forces involved and any damage or casualties were not identified; authorities are aware and investigations are ongoing; no United States or CENTCOM statement had been reported in the coverage in hand)

Nov 22, 2026 (the Revolutionary Guard Navy said two supertankers caught fire after striking naval mines in a restricted area east of the strait, north of Ghanam Island; one report said one tanker carrying more than 2 million barrels of crude sank; no vessel names, flags or casualty figures were given and the claims have not been independently verified); CNN analysis of UKMTO data, reported Nov 22, 2026 (November has at least 22 reported attacks on shipping, the second-highest monthly total since the war began, after more than 30 in October)

Nov 23, 2026 (2 commercial ships crossed on Nov 22, one inbound and one outbound, neither of them a tanker; 51 crossings in the last 7 days, a seven-day average of 7.3 a day against a pre-crisis 84.8 a day; no crossings yet on Nov 23 as of 07:39 UTC; AIS-visible only, ships running dark are not counted); Kpler via Reuters, reported Nov 22, 2026 (5 ships crossed on Nov 21 and none were recorded on Nov 22)

Nov 23, 2026 (diesel crack $77.66 and 3-2-1 crack $39.74 on the latest print dated Nov 23; all time maximum diesel crack $117.92 on Sep 16; 45 total closes above $100; current streak above $100 is zero)

Nov 20, 2026 (3d old), positions as of Nov 17 (NYMEX WTI managed money net long +15,814, down 9,900 on the week and the lowest of 2026, at about 0.8 percent of open interest; longs rose 5,519 while shorts were added, up 15,419 to 137,797, the largest short book of the year; ICE Brent managed money net long +133,635, essentially flat)
